extraction.human_system:
PRIMARY (2D, where all toxicity data comes from): human iPSC-derived forebrain neuronal cultures. Source material is control (unaffected) human neural progenitor cells, stated as "Control NPCs from a previous study were used" citing Buijsen et al., Mov Disord 2023;38:1428-1442 (the SCA1 patient-derived fibroblast/iPSC study). The specific donor identifier, sex, age and genotype are NOT stated in this paper. NPCs were expanded on Poly-D-lysine/laminin, differentiated with the STEMdiff Forebrain Neuron Differentiation Medium kit (STEMCELL Technologies) with daily medium changes to day 7, then matured with the BrainPhys hPSC Neuron kit for 2 weeks with half-medium changes every 2-3 days. Seeded at 17,000 cells/well in 50 uL (96-well, used for the imaging/toxicity readouts) or 100,000 cells/well in 500 uL (12-well). Treatment on day 11 of maturation, harvest on day 14 of maturation. The culture is a MIXED neuron/astrocyte culture: the paper reports "of the immuno-positive cells, around 40% were neurons and 60% astrocytes" (MAP2+ vs GFAP+), consistent with the brief. 2D monolayer.

SECONDARY (3D): hiPSC-derived cerebral/cortical organoids generated with the STEMdiff Cerebral Organoid Kit (STEMCELL Technologies) per the manufacturer protocol. ASO uptake experiments at day 14 or day 35 per Methods; the Results and Figure 3 label the early timepoint "D15" (a D14/D15 inconsistency within the paper, flagged, not resolved by me). D35 organoids were used for HTT and APP splice experiments (4-6 organoids per well, 29-day-old organoids added to CEM-containing wells per Methods 2.7 - another internal date inconsistency with the "day 35" statement). NO quantitative viability or toxicity assay was performed on organoids; the only 3D tolerability observation is a qualitative macroscopic morphology statement about electroporation.

All systems are human-derived and neural. No non-neural human line was used for any readout in this paper (the Huh-7/HLE/HeLa/HEK293/A549 cell lines mentioned in the Discussion are cited from reference 12, Hori et al. NAR 2015, and are NOT experiments performed here - nothing from them is extracted).
extraction.delivery_method: Four delivery methods were compared. (1) CALCIUM-ENHANCED MEDIUM (CEM) - the paper's focus: "Complete BrainPhys Neuronal medium was supplemented with 9 mM calcium chloride (CaCl2) and 2% FBS". For 3D: "2 mL of maturation medium, enhanced with 9 mM CaCl2 and 2% FBS per well". (2) GYMNOTIC / FREE UPTAKE - the same BrainPhys medium with "extra BrainPhys medium" instead of the CaCl2/FBS supplement; this is the "500nM - CEM" arm in Figure 1. (3) LIPOFECTAMINE 2000 TRANSFECTION - "ASO suspension was made with 500 nM ASO and 2.5 uL Lipofectamine 2000 incubated in 50 uL DMEM/F12 for 5 min... One hundred uL Lipofectamine/ASO mix was added to the cells and incubated at 37 C for 4 h, after which the medium was changed to complete BrainPhys Neuronal medium and incubated for a total of 72 h"; this is the "transfection" arm. (4) NEPA21 ELECTROPORATION (3D organoids only), by cuvette (CU500 chamber) or by NEPA electrode, in 100 uL Opti-MEM plus ASO; parameters in Table 2 (poring pulse 225 V, 1.5 ms, 50 ms interval, 4 pulses, 10% decay rate, + polarity; transfer pulse 20 V, 50 ms, 50 ms interval, 5 pulses, 40% decay rate, +/- polarity). No conjugates were used. Note for the dataset: CEM is a medium additive, not a covalent conjugate - the oligonucleotides themselves are unconjugated.
extraction.purity_characterization_reported:
VERBATIM, Methods section 2.5 "Antisense Oligonucleotides", complete text of that section: "All ASOs were synthesized using standard solid-phase phosphoramidite chemistry according to previously published protocols (Capaldi and Scozzari, 2007) [15] and purified using AEX-HLPC."

That is the entirety of the synthesis/purification reporting. NO supplier or vendor is named, NO purity percentage is given, NO mass spectrometry or identity confirmation is reported, NO endotoxin testing is reported, and no lot/batch information is given. Note: the article prints "AEX-HLPC"; this appears to be a typographical error for AEX-HPLC (anion-exchange HPLC), but I am recording the string exactly as printed and flagging the likely typo rather than silently correcting it. Reference 15 is Capaldi D.C., Scozzari A.N., "Manufacturing and Analytical Processes for 2-O-(2-Methoxyethyl)-Modified Oligonucleotides", in Antisense Drug Technology, 2nd ed., CRC Press, Boca Raton, FL, USA, 2007.

oligos.sequence_5to3: 5′-UCC UUU CAU CUC UGG GCU C-3′
oligos.modality: Splice-modulating (steric-block) single-stranded antisense oligonucleotide, fluorescently labelled with FAM. Used in this paper as the uptake/delivery tracer and as the test article in the only quantitative toxicity experiment.
oligos.backbone_chemistry: Phosphorothioate (stated in Table 1 as "2′-O-methoxyethyl-modified phosphorothioate"; the paper does not state whether the PS substitution is full or partial, nor the stereochemistry)
oligos.sugar_modifications: 2′-O-methoxyethyl (2′-MOE), stated as the uniform chemistry for the ASO in Table 1
oligos.base_modifications: NOT_REPORTED. The paper says nothing about 5-methylcytosine or any other nucleobase modification. Note the printed sequence uses U rather than T throughout, which is the RNA-style convention typical of uniformly 2′-modified splice-switching ASOs; I am NOT inferring any base chemistry from this.
oligos.modification_positions: NOT_REPORTED as a per-position map. Table 1's "Chemistry" column gives only the uniform motif "2′-O-methoxyethyl-modified phosphorothioate" for the whole molecule. There is no gapmer wing definition, no 5-10-5 style notation, and no per-linkage or per-sugar annotation anywhere in the paper. The sequence in Table 1 is printed in plain uppercase with spaces every three characters and no case- or symbol-based chemistry encoding, so the sequence string itself carries no positional modification information. INFERENCE (mine, flagged as such, not source content): a uniformly 2′-MOE/PS design is the expected reading of the stated motif for a steric-block splice-switching ASO, but the paper does not say so.
oligos.target_gene: NOT_REPORTED. The paper never states what H40 targets. It is introduced only as the FAM-labelled ASO used to visualise and quantify delivery. The extraction brief supplied to me described H40 as a "control", but the article itself does NOT designate it a control, scrambled or non-targeting oligonucleotide anywhere, so I am not recording that as source content.

extraction.key_findings:
1. CEM (BrainPhys + 9 mM CaCl2 + 2% FBS) delivers a 2′-MOE phosphorothioate ASO into human iPSC-derived neuronal cultures at 10-500 nM with NO significant loss of nuclei, while achieving >90% transfection efficiency in neurons at 500 nM. Authors: "CEM is an efficient and low-toxic ASO delivery method in iPSC-derived neuronal 2D cultures and 3D brain organoids."

2. The ONLY statistically significant cytotoxicity in the paper is in the Lipofectamine 2000 arm (*** p < 0.001, Figure 1B). Because the same ASO at the same 500 nM concentration is non-toxic when delivered by CEM or gymnotically on the same plate, this isolates the LIPID TRANSFECTION REAGENT as the toxic agent, not the oligonucleotide. This is a delivery-vehicle toxicity datapoint in a human neural system, which is itself useful, but it is not oligonucleotide toxicity.

3. Gymnotic/free uptake at 500 nM was well tolerated but ineffective ("Gymnotic uptake was not efficient in the concentrations used").

4. No cell-type-selective toxicity: the MAP2+ neuron / GFAP+ astrocyte ratio (~40:60) "did not significantly differ" across all six conditions. But exposure is cell-type-differential - at 500 nM + CEM, neurons are ~90% FAM-positive versus astrocytes ~55%.

5. In 3D, cuvette electroporation caused macroscopic organoid morphological changes; CEM and NEPA-electrode delivery did not.

6. MAJOR GAP for this module: organoids were dosed at 1000 nM (D15, Figure 3) and at 100,000 nM (100 uM, D35, Methods 2.7) with NO viability or toxicity assay of any kind performed at those concentrations. USABILITY VERDICT: usable=true, but with a narrow yield and important caveats.

WHAT THIS SOURCE GENUINELY CONTRIBUTES to the human_invitro CNS class: three fully sequenced 2′-MOE/PS oligonucleotides paired with a real, dose-resolved viability readout (DAPI nuclei count, n = 6) in a human iPSC-derived neuronal culture, across four delivery conditions, with an explicit authors' tolerability call. That is exactly the missing class. There are 5 dose-resolved viability rows, 1 cell-type-composition row, 2 accumulation/context rows and 1 qualitative 3D morphology row.

WHAT LIMITS IT - please propagate these downstream:

(a) EVERY VIABILITY VALUE IS FIGURE-ONLY. Figure 1B is an unlabelled scatter plot. No group means, SDs, per-point values, percent-of-control figures or effect sizes appear in the text, in any table, or in any supplement - and this article has NO supplementary material at all (confirmed two ways: zero <supplementary-material> elements in the JATS XML, and zero occurrences of the string "supplementary" anywhere in the article; the EuropePMC supplementaryFiles endpoint for this PMCID returns only the four main figure images). I did not read point heights off the plot, so every readout_value for the viability rows is NOT_REPORTED. If this dataset needs numeric viability values, they are not recoverable from this publication and would require contacting the authors.

(b) THE TOXICITY SIGNAL IS NOT OLIGONUCLEOTIDE TOXICITY. The single significant cytotoxic result belongs to Lipofectamine 2000. Same oligo, same 500 nM, same plate, non-toxic via CEM and via gymnotic uptake. Any pipeline that assigns "toxic at 500 nM" to H40 from this paper would be wrong, and the authors would say so. I have flagged this in the toxic_call and notes of that row.

(c) NO PER-POSITION MODIFICATION MAP EXISTS. Table 1's chemistry column says only "2′-O-methoxyethyl-modified phosphorothioate" for all three ASOs. There is no gapmer wing definition, no 5-10-5 style notation, no per-linkage annotation, and the printed sequences use plain uppercase with spaces every three characters and no case/symbol chemistry encoding. So the design half of the design-outcome pair is at motif resolution only, not position resolution. I did not reconstruct a uniform 2′-MOE/full-PS pattern from memory even though that is the conventional reading of the motif; I recorded it as NOT_REPORTED with my inference explicitly labelled as inference.

(d) H40 IS NOT DESIGNATED A CONTROL BY THE ARTICLE. The extraction brief I was given described H40 as "a FAM-labelled control", but the paper never calls it a control, scrambled, or non-targeting, and never states its target. I set is_control=false and target_gene=NOT_REPORTED rather than importing the brief's characterisation into the record. Flagging this explicitly because it is a discrepancy between the brief and the source, and because miscoding a test article as a control would corrupt downstream analysis.

(e) DONOR/LINE IDENTITY IS INCOMPLETE. "Control NPCs from a previous study were used", citing Buijsen et al., Mov Disord 2023;38:1428-1442. No donor ID, sex, age, or genotype in this paper. Resolving the line would require the cited paper.

(f) INTERNAL DATE INCONSISTENCIES IN THE SOURCE, not resolved by me: Methods 2.3 says organoid uptake experiments were done on "day 14 or 35", while Results 3.3 and Figure 3 say "D15"; Methods 2.7 says "Four to six 29-day-old organoids were added per well" while the corresponding Results section and Figure 4 describe D35 organoids. (g) TYPOGRAPHICAL NOTE: Methods 2.5 prints "AEX-HLPC", almost certainly a typo for AEX-HPLC. Recorded verbatim in purity_characterization_reported with the likely correction flagged, not silently fixed.

The Discussion mentions Huh-7, HLE, HeLa, HEK293 and A549 cells, but these are cited from reference 12 (Hori et al., NAR 2015) and are NOT experiments performed in this paper. Nothing from them was extracted. Every row in this record is from a human neural system.

(i) The five 2D viability rows share one plot and one control group; they are five conditions on Figure 1B, not five independent experiments. Treat them as a within-experiment dose/delivery series (n = 6 wells each).

extraction.key_findings:
The paper explicitly frames a human-neural safety assessment: "Moreover, to identify adverse effects of ASOs in human neural cells we measured their toxicity, immunogenicity and off-target effects" (Extended Data Fig. 6).

1. APOPTOSIS / TOXICITY - NEGATIVE (no ASO-induced toxicity). In dissociated TS patient hiPSC-derived cortical neurons (day 210) exposed to 1 uM ASO for 48 h, the authors report: "In both TUNEL assay and cleaved caspase 3 (c-Cas3) staining used for estimation of apoptosis we found no differences among ASO.Scr-, ASO.14- and mock-exposed neurons." The DNase positive control worked (mean 58.7% TUNEL+ vs 7.6-17.1% in all other arms), so the null result is supported by a functioning assay with real dynamic range. The significant terms in the TUNEL ANOVA (F3,20 = 13.13, P < 0.0001) are driven by the DNase positive control, not by any ASO.

2. IMMUNOGENICITY - NEGATIVE, BUT MEASURED IN A NON-NEURAL LINE. "hTLR9 reporter cells are used to evaluate the immunogenicity of exogenous DNA and we did not detect hTLR9 signalling activation following ASO delivery." ASO.14, ASO.17 and ASO.18 at 1 uM for 16-24 h were indistinguishable from water; the ODN positive control gave a ~7-fold signal. CRITICAL: this assay is in modified HEK293T cells (human embryonic kidney), NOT neural cells, so it is flagged is_neural=false and must be excluded from the CNS module.

3. OFF-TARGET TRANSCRIPTS - NEGATIVE, in human neural tissue. qPCR of CACNA1D (the closest CaV paralogue, CaV1.3), USP28, TMEM105 and DGKK in hCO exposed to 1 uM ASO for 3 days showed no significant differences (all P > 0.44). This is a safety/specificity endpoint, not a cytotoxicity endpoint, and is recorded as context.

4. NO VIABILITY ASSAY EXISTS IN THIS PAPER. The task brief anticipated a viability readout. There is none. I searched the full text for "viability", "cell death", "LDH", "ATP", "MTT", "cytokine", "inflammat", "GFAP", "microglia" - none occur. The only cytotoxicity readouts are the two apoptosis stains. Do not record a viability row for this source.

5. NO NEURITE/MORPHOLOGY TOXICITY IN VITRO. The only morphology data (Extended Data Fig. 10d-g, Golgi dendrite tracing) are from human organoid neurons TRANSPLANTED INTO RAT CORTEX with intrathecal ASO - human cells but in vivo, therefore outside human_invitro. Excluded.

6. NO CLEAN IN VITRO ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY TOLERABILITY ROW. Patch-clamp and GCaMP calcium data in TS neurons with ASO are framed as rescue of the disease phenotype (efficacy), and there is no healthy-control-plus-ASO arm, so ASO tolerability cannot be separated from disease rescue. Excluded, noted.

7. AUTHORS' OWN CAVEAT, verbatim: "Recent studies have shown that ASOs containing a gapmer design can show dose-dependent acute neurotoxicity in the central nervous system" and "Therefore, in vivo short- and long-term pharmacology will be necessary to evaluate the relative toxicity of the full MOE-modified, splicing-modulating candidates." The authors themselves regard their in vitro safety package as preliminary.
extraction.notes:
HOW THE NUMBERS WERE OBTAINED - READ THIS BEFORE USING THE ROWS.

None of the toxicity values are printed in the paper's text or in any table. Extended Data Fig. 6 is a figure-only presentation. However, the publisher released Source Data, and the Europe PMC supplementary ZIP contains it as 41586_2024_7310_MOESM13_ESM.xlsx, with sheets literally named "Ext. Data Fig. 6b", "Ext. Data Fig. 6d", "Ext. Data Fig. 6e" and "Ext. Data Fig. 6f". These sheets carry EXACT per-replicate numeric values.

Therefore, in every measurement row, readout_value is the VERBATIM list of per-replicate values copied character-for-character from that source-data spreadsheet. It is NOT a figure estimate and NOT invented. Where I state a mean and SD, it is EXPLICITLY LABELLED as "computed by extractor" - the paper never prints a mean or SD for these panels. This is derivation from released source data, not reading values off a figure, and I have kept the two clearly separated per rule 4.

INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK (my verification, not source content): the replicate counts in the source data reproduce the degrees of freedom in the published legends exactly. TUNEL: 4 groups, 3+3+9+9 = 24 observations, giving F3,20 - matches the published "F3,20 = 13.13". Caspase 3: 3 groups x 3 = 9, giving F2,6 - matches "F2,6 = 0.03288". Off-target: 5 groups x 3 = 15, giving F4,10 - matches "F4,10". This confirms the spreadsheet is the true source data for those panels.

SEQUENCES - THE CENTRAL LIMITATION. No ASO sequence is printed anywhere: not in the main text, not in Methods, not in any Extended Data legend, and not in the 21-page Supplementary Information PDF. Supplementary Table 1, which the paper directs the reader to for sequences, contains ONLY PCR and qPCR primers (NGS primers, GAPDH, exon 8/8A qPCR, rat primers, cloning primers, and the off-target assay primers for DGKK, TMEM105, Cav1.3 and USP28). All ASO sequences are NOT_REPORTED. I did not reconstruct any from memory.

MODIFICATION ARCHITECTURE - SOURCE VS INFERENCE. The SOURCE states: 20-nt, phosphorothioate backbone, "a MOE modification", 5-methylcytosine used instead of cytosine. The SOURCE also refers in the Discussion to "the full MOE-modified, splicing-modulating candidates" and contrasts them with "ASOs containing a gapmer design". MY INFERENCE, clearly labelled as inference: these are uniformly 2'-MOE-modified steric-block splice-switching ASOs with no DNA gap, i.e. RNase H-independent - which is consistent with their mechanism (redirecting CACNA1C splicing from exon 8A to exon 8) and with Extended Data Fig. 4 showing total CaV1.2 protein is unchanged (F4,31 = 0.3548, P = 0.8387). A per-position modification map is NOT_REPORTED and I have not fabricated one.

TUNEL ANOVA - DO NOT MISREAD THE ASTERISKS. The legend reports "F3,20 = 13.13, P < 0.0001; ****P < 0.0001, **P = 0.0033" for the TUNEL panel. These significant post-hoc comparisons are against the DNase positive control, NOT evidence of ASO toxicity. The authors' own sentence is unambiguous: "no differences among ASO.Scr-, ASO.14- and mock-exposed neurons." Any downstream pipeline that reads the panel-level P value alone would wrongly score ASO.14 as toxic. All ASO rows are therefore effect_direction = no_change.

TUNEL DIRECTIONALITY ODDITY. From the source data, ASO.14 (extractor-computed mean 7.61%) and ASO.Scr (11.70%) both sit BELOW the water/mock arm (17.06%). Taken at face value the ASOs slightly reduce TUNEL positivity relative to mock. The authors do not comment on this and the mock arm has only n=3 versus n=9 for the ASO arms, so I regard this as noise and NOT as a protective effect. Recorded here as uncertainty rather than smoothed over.

hTLR9 BATCH DRIFT - IMPORTANT FOR ANYONE POOLING THE VALUES. The three independent experiments have very different absolute baselines (water arm means approx. 0.635, 0.214 and 0.150 OD respectively). Pooling all nine replicates gives a large SD that reflects batch drift, not treatment variance. Within EVERY individual experiment, every ASO arm is essentially identical to the water arm, while the ODN positive control is 3.6x to 17x higher. The negative immunogenicity conclusion is robust within-experiment. I report both the pooled figure and the per-experiment means so this is not hidden. Again: this assay is in HEK293T cells and is flagged is_neural=false.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY DID NOT TURN INTO ROWS, AND WHY:
- Extended Data Fig. 4b, CaV1.2 western blot in ASO-treated hCO (F4,31 = 0.3548, P = 0.8387, n = 6-8). Human neural and in vitro, but this is a target-protein-level readout confirming the splice-switch does not deplete total CaV1.2. It is a mechanism/specificity control, not a toxicity endpoint.
- Extended Data Fig. 5b and Fig. 2b/2c/2e, exon 8A/exon 8 qPCR splicing. Pure efficacy/knockdown. Excluded per the brief.
- Extended Data Fig. 10d-g, Golgi dendrite morphology (area under curve, intersection peak radius, longest dendrite length, total dendrite length; n = 24/24/11 neurons). Human neurons but transplanted into rat cortex with intrathecal ASO - in vivo, not human_invitro.
- Extended Data Fig. 9, rat cortex/cerebellum/spinal cord qPCR. Rat tissue, excluded.
- Patch-clamp voltage-dependent inactivation and GCaMP residual calcium. Framed as rescue of the TS phenotype (efficacy), and there is no healthy-control-plus-ASO arm, so ASO tolerability cannot be disentangled from disease correction. I note that the GCaMP dose-response did extend to 10 uM ASO (Extended Data Fig. 8g source data columns Het_ASO14_10, Het_ASO17_10, Het_ASO18_10) without the authors reporting any adverse effect, but since they never analyse it as a tolerability endpoint I will not manufacture one.
- Cy5-ASO flow cytometry uptake. The paper states only "Most cells, including CD90-expressing neurons, were Cy5+" with NO quantified percentage in the text. The Supplementary Figure 1 gating plot shows quadrant labels (Q1 39.0, Q2 60.1, Q3 0.27) but these are a gating illustration, not a reported uptake statistic, so I have not created an accumulation row rather than risk fabricating one.

ASO.20 HAS NO TOXICITY DATA. It appears only in the splicing screen (Fig. 2c source data, 41586_2024_7310_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx). It is listed in the oligos array for completeness but generates no measurement row.

CONCENTRATION CEILING. Every toxicity measurement here is at a SINGLE concentration, 1 uM. There is no cytotoxicity dose-response. The 0.001-10 uM range quoted in the paper applies to splicing efficacy and calcium rescue, not to any toxicity assay. So this source cannot support a cytotoxicity threshold or NOAEL; toxic_call is "non-toxic at 1 uM" and nothing stronger should be inferred.

OVERALL VALUE JUDGEMENT: this is a genuine human in vitro CNS tolerability dataset - patient-derived hiPSC cortical neurons, an explicit adverse-effect assessment, exact per-replicate source-data numbers, and a permissive CC BY 4.0 licence. Its weakness is that it is entirely negative at one concentration, and that the design side is incomplete because no sequences are disclosed.

PRIMARY HUMAN NEURAL SYSTEM: SH-SY5Y human neuroblastoma cell line, 2D monolayer, transformed/immortalised. NO differentiation protocol is reported anywhere in the paper (no retinoic acid, BDNF, or any maturation step is described), so the cells are presumed undifferentiated; the paper does not state this explicitly. No maturation age. No supplier, catalogue number, passage number or authentication reported. This is the ONLY human neural system in the paper.

NON-NEURAL HUMAN COMPARATOR (is_neural=false rows): HEK293 APPswe. Verbatim from Methods: "HEK293-APPswe cells are a stable cell line generated by transfecting HEK293 cells with a complementary DNA (cDNA) construct encoding human APP with the Swedish mutation (APPswe) K595N/M596L located near the beta-secretase 1 (BACE1) cleavage site of the APP." Human embryonic kidney origin - EXCLUDED from the neural class per module rules.

NOT PRESENT: no iPSC-derived neurons, no iPSC donor or genotype, no organoids, no astrocytes, no microglia, no neural progenitors, no BBB model, no 3D culture. The authors themselves flag this as a limitation, stating that "More physiologically relevant systems (e.g., induced pluripotent stem cell [iPSC]-derived neurons or in vivo models) will be required" and that "immortalized cell lines present a restricted dynamic range". Treat the SH-SY5Y rows as the weakest tier of "human in vitro CNS": human and neural-lineage, but a cancer line, undifferentiated, lipofected.
extraction.key_findings:
USABLE, but the per-compound toxicity coverage is far narrower than the task brief anticipated.

1. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF - only 2 of the 11 bispecific ASOs have any human neural viability data. The brief asked for "the per-compound threshold for every one of the 11". The paper does not contain that. All 11 bispecific ASOs (APGS, BACD, BAMT, BAPP1, BAPP2, BAPP3, BATA, GRAGSB, GRANO, GRBCA, GSBGRB) were screened ONLY for target knockdown by qPCR at a single 20 nM dose (Figures 1 and 2), which is an efficacy readout and does not count. MTS viability was run on exactly two of them, APGS and BAMT, the two lead compounds. I grepped every occurrence of "viabilit|cytotox|toxic|MTS" in the full text to confirm this; there is no viability panel for the other nine.

2. CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF - the MTS dose range is NOT 0.1-100 nM. Reading the axes of Figure 4D/4H directly, the SH-SY5Y viability doses are UT, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 nM. Figure 3D/3H (HEK293) adds a 10 nM point: UT, 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 nM. The 0.1-100 nM (log -1 to 2) range belongs to the IC50 knockdown panels (A, B, E, F), not the viability panels.

3. THE TWO HUMAN NEURAL DOSE-RESPONSE RESULTS (SH-SY5Y, MTS, 48 h) - these are the headline rows and they separate the two leads cleanly:
   - BAMT (BACE1 + MTOR, 13-mer LNA gapmer): "no reduction in cell viability at any dose tested (up to 100 nM, Figure 4D)". Clean up to 100 nM.
   - APGS (APP + GSK3beta, 14-mer LNA gapmer): "dose-dependent reduction in cell viability was significant at doses >40 nM (Figure 4H)". Toxic.
   The same two compounds behave differently again in the non-neural HEK293 comparator, and importantly the ranking is preserved but the potency of the toxicity shifts: BAMT drops viability only at 80 and 100 nM in HEK293 (Figure 3D) while being clean at 100 nM in SH-SY5Y; APGS drops viability from 20 nM onwards in HEK293 (Figure 3H) versus 40 nM in SH-SY5Y. So the neural line is the MORE tolerant of the two systems for both compounds - a cell-type-dependence worth carrying into the dataset.

4. TEXT vs FIGURE DISCREPANCY ON APGS, flagged and not smoothed over. The Results text says the APGS viability drop was significant at doses ">40 nM". The Figure 4H panel itself carries a "**" significance asterisk ON the 40 nM bar (then "***" at 60, 80 and 100 nM). So the figure indicates significance begins AT 40 nM, not above it. I have recorded the authors' written threshold in toxic_call and the per-bar asterisk in each row's notes, and I have not reconciled them.

5. SIX COMPOUNDS GET A SINGLE-DOSE HUMAN NEURAL VIABILITY CALL. Figures S7D and S8D are previously-unremarked MTS panels in SH-SY5Y at 20 nM covering APGS, BAMT, and four single-gene ASOs (APP-3, GSK3beta-2, BACE1-2, mTOR-3), plus two-ASO combinations at 10 and 20 nM each. Table S2 gives all 23 ASOs with explicit per-position LNA notation ("+" prefixes a locked base), so the exact gapmer architecture is recoverable for every compound rather than just a stated motif - unusually good for this dataset. All are fully phosphorothioate 3-LNA / DNA-gap / 3-LNA gapmers. Gap lengths are 7-10 DNA; note GRAGSB has a 10-nt DNA gap, which exceeds the "7-9 DNA monomers" the supplement itself claims. 8. NEGATIVE CONTROL SEQUENCE IS MISSING. The "NC" negative control ASO is used as the comparator throughout and appears in the S7D/S8D viability panels, but its sequence is not printed in Table S2 or anywhere else. extraction.notes:
SCOPE AND WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED
- Neuro2A (Figure 6D, mBAMT viability, "Reduction in cell viability was only significant at the 100 nM dose") is MURINE and was excluded entirely - no row created. The mBAMT oligo is still listed in the oligos array for design completeness, but it carries no human measurement.
- Figures 1 and 2 (the 20 nM screen of all 11 bispecific ASOs in HEK293 APPswe and SH-SY5Y) are qPCR target-knockdown only. Efficacy, not toxicity - no rows created. I verified by grepping every occurrence of "viabilit|cytotox|toxic|MTS" across the full text that no viability panel exists for the nine non-lead bispecific ASOs.
- IC50 knockdown values, Abeta42 ELISA reductions, tau pS396 changes and HN1 off-target qPCR are all efficacy/specificity readouts, not toxicity, and were not entered as measurements. Two are noted as context: tau pS396 in SH-SY5Y (Figures S6-S8) is arguably a neuronal protein-state readout, but the authors describe it as a downstream pharmacodynamic effect of intended GSK3beta/MTOR silencing, not a toxicity, and report only "modest" non-significant changes. I did not force it into the toxicity class.

WHY 24 MEASUREMENT ROWS AND NOT 11
The brief expected per-ASO viability thresholds for all 11 bispecific ASOs in Figure 4. That data does not exist. Figure 4 characterises exactly two compounds (APGS, BAMT), which is what its own legend says. The 11-compound number in the brief comes from the DESIGN panel (11 bispecific ASOs designed and screened for knockdown), not from the viability work. Human neural viability calls exist for 6 distinct compounds plus 2 combinations plus 1 control.

SEQUENCE PROVENANCE AND INTEGRITY
- All 23 sequences transcribed character-for-character from Table S2 in Supplementary Document S1 (mmc1.pdf, pp.2-3), preserving the "+" LNA prefix convention and the "/IDSP/" abasic spacer tokens exactly as printed, including the uppercase form "/IDSP/" used in the table (the table's own caption refers to it in lowercase as "idSp").
- Independently verified: the identical set of 23 sequences was recovered from mmc3.pdf (Document S2, article plus supplemental information). A sorted set diff between the two extractions is empty. No sequence was reconstructed, inferred, or recalled from memory.
- Table S2 does not explicitly state 5'->3' orientation; the column header is simply "Sequence". Standard convention is assumed but is NOT stated by the source. Flagged.
- The one other nucleotide string in the paper, "CATTGTCTCTAAC" (Results, target-specificity section), is the HN1 GENOMIC OFF-TARGET SITE that differs from BAMT's target by one nucleotide. It is NOT the BAMT ASO sequence and must not be used as such.

CHEMISTRY - FULLY POSITIONAL, WHICH IS THE MAIN VALUE OF THIS SOURCE
Verbatim from the Table S2 caption: "All LNA-ASOs contained a fully phosphorothioated backbone with 7-9 DNA monomers flanked at both ends by three or more LNA-modified nucleotides (+ indicates an LNA-modified base). The BAPP2 and BAPP3 ASOs included one or two abasic sites (idSp)."
Verbatim from Methods: "gapmer ASOs were designed with a fully phosphorothioated backbone, consisting of a core region of 7-9 DNA bases flanked by three LNA-modified nucleotides (LNAs) at each end".
Because the "+" notation is per-position, exact LNA/DNA positions are recoverable for all 23 compounds and I have recorded them. Every compound is 3 LNA / n DNA / 3 LNA.
DISCREPANCY I DID NOT SMOOTH OVER: the source claims a 7-9 DNA core, but parsing the printed notation gives a 10-nt DNA gap for GRAGSB (+C+A+A AAAGATATTC +A+G+A). GRAGSB falls outside the stated design rule. It has no toxicity data, so this does not affect any measurement row.

OTHER SOURCE INCONSISTENCIES OBSERVED (recorded, not corrected)
- Gene-panel size: Results says ASOs were designed "from a set of 20 genes"; Methods says "Eighteen potential gene targets". Both cite Table S1.
- Coordinate/length mismatches in Table S2 for two single-gene ASOs: APP-1 has 13 nt printed but a 14-nt coordinate span (Chr21: 26096006-26096019); BACE1-1 has 15 nt printed but a 14-nt span (Chr11: 117310519-117310532). I report the SEQUENCE as printed and length_nt as counted from that sequence; the coordinates may be off by one. Neither compound has toxicity data.
- MTOR-4 coordinates print as "Chr1: 111112097-111112009" (end < start, and inconsistent in magnitude with the other MTOR entries which are ~11.1-11.2 Mb). Almost certainly a typographical error in the source. Reported verbatim, not corrected. No toxicity data for this compound.
- Naming varies between Table S2 and the figures: GSK3B-2 / "GSK3beta-2", MTOR-3 / "mTOR-3". Same compounds. I used the Table S2 form as local_name and noted the figure form.

STATISTICAL AND DESIGN LIMITATIONS AFFECTING EVERY ROW
- n = 3 biological replicates for all viability panels. Methods say "at least three independent biological replicates". Underpowered for a toxicity threshold.
- Single timepoint only: 48 h post-transfection. No longer exposure, no washout, no recovery.
- Single readout modality: MTS (mitochondrial/NAD(P)H-dependent dehydrogenase reduction) only. NO LDH, no caspase/apoptosis, no ATP, no neurite or morphology, no electrophysiology, no cytokines, no nuclear-inclusion or mislocalisation readout. MTS is a metabolic proxy and cannot distinguish cytostatic from cytotoxic effects, or reduced proliferation from cell death - relevant since SH-SY5Y is a proliferating cancer line and the assay kit is sold as a "Cell Proliferation Assay".
- No positive cytotoxicity control is reported for any viability panel.
- Delivery is lipofection throughout, so these are not free-uptake tolerability data.
- Normalisation basis for "relative 490 nM absorbance" is not stated explicitly (UT appears to be the anchor in Figures 3/4; NC appears to be the anchor in S7D/S8D). Flagged as an inconsistency between main and supplementary panels.

DATA AVAILABILITY
"Data are available upon request to the corresponding author." No repository, no accession, no deposited source data. Underlying numeric values for the viability figures are therefore not publicly obtainable, which is why every readout_value is NOT_REPORTED rather than recoverable with more effort.

extraction.purity_characterization_reported:
PARTIAL. Verbatim from Materials and methods, 'ASO design': "Candidate bispecific ASOs were synthesized by IDT (Integrated DNA Technologies) and purified by high-performance liquid chromatography".

That is the entirety of the synthesis/purification reporting. NOT REPORTED anywhere in the article or either supplementary PDF: numeric purity percentage, mass spectrometry / ESI-MS confirmation of identity, HPLC trace or retention data, endotoxin testing, residual solvent or metal content, lot numbers, salt form, quantitation method, or storage/reconstitution conditions. It is also not stated whether the single-gene comparator ASOs (APP-1/2/3, BACE1-1/2, GSK3B-1/2, MTOR-1/2/3/4) or the mouse mBAMT were made and purified the same way - the sentence names only the "candidate bispecific ASOs". The negative control ASO's source and purification are likewise unstated.

Duplex melting temperatures ARE reported per compound in Table S2, but these are COMPUTED, not measured. Verbatim from the Table S2 caption: "Duplex melting temperatures (Tm) were calculated using the Qiagen GeneGlobe Tm prediction tool (https://geneglobe.qiagen.com/us/tools/tm-prediction), which applies a nearest-neighbor model based on canonical phosphodiester backbones.
